reasoning_summary: The deterministic verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with no failed checks, so ACCEPT is not allowed. REJECT is not justified either, because no FAIL has been measured.
All five uncertainty components (averaging, statistics, mesh, time, domain) are unmeasured for both mean_drag_coefficient and strouhal_number.
R0 is not shown to be in a sustained limit cycle. The physics_regime check is INCONCLUSIVE because the lift amplitude changes by +25.8% across the analysed window.
The stationary window start (15.276) is the MSER cap (stationary_window_start_is_mser_cap = true). The window has only 3 cycles, and the record ends at 39.99 convective units.
The drag statistics are unreliable. The 95% CI is 0.044509 on a mean of 1.3039. The relative drift is 0.040105, which is above the 0.03 tolerance. The Strouhal statistical uncertainty is 3.58%.

The submitted-setup drag (1.2961) and the stationary-window drag (1.3039) differ. The Strouhal numbers also differ: 0.16129 and 0.16058 (window), against an FFT value of 0.16169. These differences are comparable to the tolerance, so the transient is contaminating the statistics.

Mesh, time-step and domain studies would each compare against a parent that has not reached a stationary state. Any difference would mix discretisation error with transient drift. RUN_LONGER must come first.
RUN_LONGER is the cheapest option on the menu (979 s, against 1040, 1567 and 1812 s). It also removes the blocking INCONCLUSIVE items in the physics_regime, averaging and statistics checks at once.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The wake instability is still growing at t=40 D/U. The lift amplitude has not saturated, and the 15.276 stationary-window start is a cap, not a true onset of stationarity. Extending the run will show the amplitude saturating and the mean drag settling. The mean drag may shift by more than the 0.03 tolerance relative to the R0 window values.
hypotheses.test: RUN_LONGER on R0. Check whether the lift-amplitude trend flattens, whether the drag drift falls well below 0.03, and whether the drag CI95 and Strouhal uncertainty fall below half the tolerance once at least 4 stationary cycles are available.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The Strouhal estimates are limited by frequency resolution and the short window, not by the physics. The reported frequency resolution is 0.033333, and the window and FFT values differ by about 0.001. A longer record will tighten the estimates.
hypotheses.test: After RUN_LONGER, compare the window-based and FFT Strouhal numbers and their resolution. They should agree and their resolution should improve.

next_experiment.reason: R0 has not demonstrated a sustained limit cycle. Lift amplitude changes by +25.8% across the window, the stationary window has 3 cycles (<4) and starts at the MSER cap, and the drag drift is 0.040105. Until the transient has ended, no mesh, time or domain comparison is interpretable. This is also the cheapest menu entry at 979 s.
next_experiment.expected_outcome: The lift amplitude saturates and the drag drift falls below the tolerance. The stationary window then has many more cycles, so the statistical and averaging components can be quantified for both mean drag and Strouhal number. If the amplitude or mean drag shifts markedly, R0's quantities are contaminated by the transient. This also gives a trustworthy parent for the subsequent mesh, time-step and domain experiments.

reasoning_summary: The deterministic verdict is INCONCLUSIVE and failed_checks is empty. ACCEPT is not allowed, and REJECT is not justified because no FAIL has been measured.

RUN_LONGER (R1) resolved the transient. R1 has 12 stationary cycles, drag drift 0.0001195, CI95 3.4541e-05, and the FFT and window Strouhal numbers agree at 0.16343. The statistics component now PASSES for both quantities.

R0's submitted-setup values were biased against R1's stationary window. Drag bias is 2.631% (1.2961 against 1.3311) and Strouhal bias is 1.312%. These biases are measured and are added linearly to the budget.
Averaging bias uses 0.02631 of the 0.03 drag tolerance. Only about 0.0037 is left for the root-sum-square of mesh, time and domain. This is very tight for R0 as submitted.
The physics_regime check is still INCONCLUSIVE. It references R0's +25.8% lift-amplitude change. R1 now supplies a longer record with 12 cycles, but the check has not been re-evaluated on it.
Mesh, time and domain components are all unmeasured for both quantities.

The mesh is the most likely source of an error larger than tolerance. The representative cell size is 0.45745 D, the wake has 111 streamwise cells ending at 1.0209 D, and R1 has the same 30580-cell mesh. The cylinder has 160 cells around it and the first wall cell is 0.005 D.

Time and domain look less likely to change the answer by more than 3%. dt is 0.01 convective units with second-order backward differencing, max Courant is 0.73373, and there are 611.87 steps per shedding period. The domain is 30 D upstream, 50 D downstream and 40 D half-height, with blockage 0.0125.

Budget: 2.5 of 12 relative compute is used. REFINE_MESH costs 1812 s, about 4.63 root units, so it is affordable. After it, domain (about 2.66) fits, but time (about 4.0) would not. Together, mesh, time and domain cannot all be afforded. The most informative single experiment should go first, because a demonstrated change above tolerance would be a FAIL.
Use R1 as parent. It is the only run with a verified stationary window, so differences against it reflect spatial error and not transient or sampling noise.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The coarse mesh (cell size 0.45745 D, wake cells up to 1.0209 D) biases mean drag and Strouhal number by more than the tolerance. This would show as a change under refinement larger than 0.5 x 0.03 against R1's stationary values of 1.3311 and 0.16343.
hypotheses.test: REFINE_MESH on R1 with factor 1.4142. Compare stationary-window drag and Strouhal number against R1. A change above 1.5% marks the mesh component as failing its budget. A change above 3% beyond 2x noise would be a FAIL.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The time-step and domain errors are small compared with the mesh error. Courant is below 1 and the boundaries are far from the cylinder.
hypotheses.test: If budget remains after the mesh run, run EXPAND_DOMAIN (the cheapest remaining entry at 1040 s) on R1 and compare stationary-window values.

next_experiment.reason: R1 gives a verified stationary reference (12 cycles, drift 0.0001195). Mesh is the largest unmeasured component, given the representative cell size of 0.45745 D and a wake that ends in 1.0209 D cells. Using R1 as parent keeps the comparison free of transient and sampling effects.
next_experiment.expected_outcome: The stationary-window drag and Strouhal number change little (below about 1.5%), which makes the mesh component pass its budget. If the change exceeds the 3% tolerance, the verifier records a FAIL and the root run is REJECTED.
